messages:
Alex (oncall): Heads up, I'm getting customer escalations about slow tails on /v1/generate at ~13:42 UTC. p95 jumped from ~700ms to ~1.9s, p99 hitting ~3.6s. Error rate unchanged. Opening thread to coordinate.

metrics-bot: Alert: rolling_p99(/v1/generate) = 3.6s (5m), triggered at 2026-03-15T13:44:00Z.

Lina (support): Tickets 10012, 10015, 10021 — multiple customers reporting interactive UI hangs. Some on Hosted, a couple on Dedicated. They mention longer prompts amplify the issue.

Priya (sre): Can we get a recent deploy diff? Any runtime/kernel/ batching changes in the last 3 hours?

deploy-bot: Deploy event: inference-runtime image sha: b7c9f11 pushed at 2026-03-15T12:50:13Z, rollout started at 2026-03-15T13:05:00Z (canary->prod).

Casey (infra): That image includes new adaptive-batching: it increases batch wait up to 60ms under low throughput to improve GPU utilization. Canary looked fine though. Rolled to 70% prod at ~13:05.

Priya (sre): Hmm. Adaptive batching increasing wait would raise tail for many small interactive requests. Also seeing client retries from frontend spiking; that amplifies the queue.

Jordan (frontend): Confirming: spikes in front-end retry storms after 1s timeouts. Client currently uses retry with exponential backoff starting 200ms. We'll push a quick client change to add jitter and backoff cap.

Alex (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) immediate protection (circuit-breaker / token concurrency cap), 2) undo adaptive-batching config in prod, 3) fallback routing to eu-west region for affected customers, 4) gather traces. Casey — can you toggle the batching config back to safe value (12ms) across prod?

Casey (infra): I can. Executing: `kubectl -n inference set env deployment/inference-runtime BATCH_ADAPTIVE_MAX_MS=12 --overwrite` Doing a rolling restart on pods in small batches to avoid warm-start spike.

deploy-bot: Roll config change applied to 25% of pods.

Priya (sre): While Casey is toggling, I'll apply a per-token concurrency circuit-breaker at the gateway: `token_concurrency_limit=6` with strict 429s and header `X-Rate-Limit-Reason:concurrency`. Also set `Retry-After` in seconds. This will immediately limit noisy tokens.

ops-bot: Gateway rule applied to ingress at 13:50 UTC: token_concurrency_limit=6 for /v1/generate.

Lina (support): I'll message affected customers about temporary 429s and advise decreasing parallel sessions until we stabilize.

Jordan (frontend): Client change pushed to canary: add random jitter +/- 200ms and cap retries to 3. Should reduce retry storms.

metrics-bot: After initial changes: p95 = 1.1s, p99 = 1.9s, queue depth decreasing on pods with config toggled.

Priya (sre): I'm starting targeted tracing: enabling `emit_batch_metadata=true` on a subset of runtime pods for 15 minutes. Use `kubectl exec` to flip the endpoint `POST /_debug/config` on pod. Also collecting Jaeger spans for requests that saw >500ms server-side wait.

Casey (infra): Rolling toggle complete across all exhaustion-sensitive pods. No immediate crash. Pods show improved tail.

metrics-bot: p99 now at 1.2s, trending down.

Priya (sre): Early trace analysis: batch boundaries frequently at 40-60ms in the adaptive mode; many interactive requests waited for the next batch boundary. When retries are in play, those wait times compound. Example trace: request_id=7f2b -> enqueue_wait=98ms -> batch_size=48 -> kernel_exec=5ms -> total server wait ~110ms; with client-side retry it became 3s end-to-end for some users.

Alex (oncall): Sounds like root cause. Longer-term: limit how much adaptive batching can increase wait for low-latency models; and require a perf canary when changing batching heuristics. Priya, list concrete guardrails we should add.

Priya (sre): Proposed guardrails: 1) block any deploy changing batching heuristics unless canary synthetic p99 test passes for short-prompt workload. 2) fail deploy if p99 in canary increases >12%. 3) default gateway token concurrency = 8 for self-serve; 4) routing fallback rules: auto-route to quantized variant or to another region if p99 exceeds threshold for 5m. 5) telemetry: emit BATCH_WAIT_MS, BATCH_ENTER_TS, BATCH_SIZE for 30d in debug window.

Casey (infra): I'll open INFRA-2610 to add preflight in CI for config flags and INFRA-2611 to add a deploy breaker that validates p99 synthetic.

Jordan (frontend): Note for product: we should show nicer client-visible messaging when 429 occurs and have client SDKs respect X-Rate-Limit headers. I'll coordinate with SDK team.

Lina (support): KB update: recommended client settings to avoid exacerbating tails: concurrency per-token <= 6, max retries 3, use jitter, backoff base 300ms. I'll publish steps and repro.

Priya (sre): Repro steps for engineers: 1) spin up 150 concurrent short requests (avg tokens 20) using 15 clients, 2) set client timeout 1s to provoke retry, 3) observe server logs for `BATCH_WAIT_MS` and `BATCH_SIZE`. Sample load command: 

```
seq 1 150 | xargs -n1 -P150 -I{} curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input": "hi","max_tokens":20}' &
wait
```

Check runtime log lines: `/var/log/inference/runtime.log` grep `BATCH_WAIT_MS` and `BATCH_SIZE`. Use jaeger UI to view traces with tag `batch=true`.

Priya (sre): Also recommend adding a synthetic canary job: short-prompt runner that measures p50/p95/p99 every minute and fails deploy if p99 degrades.

metrics-bot: p99 stabilized at 0.95s after 25 minutes.

Alex (oncall): Excellent. Actions summary before closing:
- Casey: completed rollback of adaptive batching and filed INFRA-2610/2611.
- Priya: will implement canary test and SLO guard proposals; drafting postmortem.
- Jordan: client retry patch in canary; push to prod after 1h if stable.
- Lina: customer communications and KB updates.

Alex (oncall): Leaving this with Priya for follow-ups. If p99 > 2s again for 10m, reopen and page infra. Marking mitigated for now.

--- Mitigation playbook (copy/paste):
1) Verify deploy diff and recent config changes (deploy-bot).
2) If batching heuristics changed, revert to safe defaults or smaller max-wait (12ms).
3) Apply temporary token-level circuit-breaker (concurrency limit + 429 + Retry-After header).
4) Redirect traffic: fallback to quantized model or alternate region for affected tiers.
5) Reduce client-side retries and add jitter (coordinate with frontend/SDK).
6) Gather traces and runtime batch logs (`BATCH_WAIT_MS`, `BATCH_SIZE`, `BATCH_ENTER_TS`).
7) Run synthetic short-prompt canary to validate p99.
8) If necessary, scale Dedicated pools or divert heavy keys to Dedicated nodes.

--- Short SLO guardrails to add to roadmap:
- Deploy-time synthetic p99 test for interactive prompt profile.
- Config change policy: blocking guard on changes to batching/kernels without canary verification.
- Default per-token concurrency limit and backpressure header.
- Routing fallback templates by model.

End of thread.
